A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniPixel. Their main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable matching of methods, experiments, and results.

before.justification: v1 reports original UniPixel benchmark evaluations, PixelQA experiments, ablations, and qualitative predictions in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, revises reported 7B results, and adds 7B MVBench results in Table 13.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same prompt encoders, object memory bank, SAM 2.1 mask decoder, inference procedure, losses, and three-stage training recipe. Revised scores do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: The training datasets in Table 12 and evaluation tasks and datasets are unchanged, including PixelQA and MVBench. Adding a 7B MVBench row does not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged within Tables 1–10 and 13. Citation changes do not add or remove evaluated baselines; the added MVBench row is another UniPixel variant.

E3.justification: Table 13 extends the reported MVBench model-size comparison from UniPixel-3B to both 3B and 7B. Existing splits, metrics, prompt conditions, preprocessing, and training settings are unchanged; the PDFs do not attribute revised scores to protocol changes.

E4.justification: The task-unification, memory-bank, encoder/decoder, training-stage, token-count, projector, and training-data ablations in Tables 11 and 14–17 are unchanged. The qualitative cases are retained; Figure 10 corrects their presentation rather than adding an analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the benchmark results. The added MVBench row follows the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: The 7B results throughout Tables 1–10 are revised under unchanged stated settings. GroundMoRe J&F changes from 47.6 to 37.8, and mixed-prompt PixelQA J&F from 61.1 to 44.9. VideoRefer-BenchD averages fall from 3.47/3.48 to 3.37/3.36, reversing the advantage over VideoRefer's unchanged 3.42/3.46. Some scores increase, including MeViS val J&F from 54.7 to 55.8. Table 13 adds 7B MVBench results averaging 64.3; existing 3B results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical task formulation, prompt representations, and training objectives are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified referring and segmentation, the object memory bank, mutual reinforcement, state-of-the-art performance, and the novel PixelQA task. These claims are not revised alongside the changed scores.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, result interpretations, and Appendix C limitations remain unchanged, including limited task coverage and first-frame mask propagation. No new explanation or qualification addresses the revised 7B outcomes.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same hardware, learning rates, batch sizes, resolutions, frame sampling, LoRA settings, initialization, and data preparation details. Project and dataset access information and licensing disclosures are also unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds five neuroimaging references alongside the new 'human-like' wording and two references concerning OCR and layout generation. It removes the Claude 3.7 system card and PerceptionGPT references. The principal comparison with earlier referring and segmentation research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits include updated institutional affiliations, the 'human-like' descriptor, small related-work wording changes, and bibliographic style adjustments. The main narrative, section order, and appendix organization remain substantially identical.

P2.justification: Table 13 gains a 7B row, with limited surrounding reflow. Figure 10 corrects the interchanged descriptions of the car and shopper videos. Ranking emphasis in several tables is updated, while the overall figure and table organization is retained.

improvement.justification: The added 7B MVBench results and corrected Figure 10 pairings improve completeness and clarity. However, substantial 7B score revisions are unexplained, and Section 4.1 still reports 64.0 ReVOS J&F although Table 1 now gives 63.7. The changed description-ranking results also receive no revised interpretation. These benefits and new reporting inconsistencies leave the net quality change uncertain.
